metadata.description: Glucose → 2 pyruvate; HK2-rate-limited in tumour cells (Warburg).
Acetyl-CoA oxidation; SDH (Complex II) ties TCA to ETC.
Growth-factor → PI3K → AKT → mTORC1; oncogenic when constitutively on.
~95% bear KRAS-G12D/V; exemplar of oncogene-addicted cancer.
Hanahan & Weinberg hallmark; TP53 loss is canonical driver.

nodes.label: siTP53 in HEK293 → reduced apoptosis after etoposide
siTP53 in HeLa → reduced apoptosis after etoposide (replication)
siKRAS in A549 → loss of anchorage-independent growth
siHK2 in HeLa → ~60% drop in lactate efflux (Warburg attenuated)
siSDHB in HEK293 → succinate accumulation + pseudohypoxia
siMYC in A549 → glycolytic + glutaminolytic flux drop
siPIK3CA in HeLa → AKT phospho-S473 collapse (>80%)
Vander Heiden et al. (2009) — Warburg revisited
Hingorani et al. (2003) — KRAS-G12D pancreatic model
Phase II trial of adagrasib (MRTX849, KRAS-G12C inhibitor) in NSCLC
Phase I/II trial of alpelisib (PIK3CA inhibitor) in HR+ breast cancer

edges.evidence: siTP53 efficiently causes apoptosis evasion under genotoxic stress (Vogelstein 2000)
KRAS knockdown reverses pancreatic-ca tumourigenicity (Singh et al. 2009)
PIK3CA knockdown causally collapses PI3K-AKT-mTOR axis activity
HK2 knockdown drops glycolytic flux ≈60% — direct metabolic effect
SDHB knockdown accumulates succinate — TCA-cycle blockade (Selak et al. 2005)
MYC knockdown drops glycolytic flux (and glutaminolysis); dual metabolic effect

BIO-EXP-007 (PIK3CA dependency) is the preclinical SPECIFICATION for alpelisib trial NCT03634332
